it is also like the lion king devouring its prey, leaving not a shred of meat behind. Yet, if one’s realization is not genuine, [it will all be in vain].
Your entry into the Way was not correct; you have not yet escaped injuring the wind or defiling the hands. Are you not afraid?
Master Fazhou, having caught a glimpse of something by the sound of the sounding-block, was like a dragon finding water—he immediately stirred up waves and billows.

Standing vividly and without dependence, he responded to stimuli with total liberation, like spring winds blowing through the flowers and willows, appearing ever more fresh. At that time, the Double-Tufted Peak (Shuangji Feng) was settled.
In which land do you reside? Do you not recognize that you have once beheld this old man’s face?
This concludes the postscript by Yuanxin of Qianzhi-an on the preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Nanshi of Mount Jing.
In my thirtieth year, I encountered the turmoil at the end of the Yuan dynasty and withdrew into mountain ravines.

There, I was able to meet Master Yigan Ji of Mount Jing and inquire about the essentials of Chan. Because my nature was somewhat sharp, he tirelessly guided me toward awakening and appointed me as his recorder.
Having served at the Master’s side for three years, I was able to taste a morsel from the cauldron and thus come to know its flavor.

At that time, among the venerable elders of the Chan forests east and west of the Zhe River—such as Liaoyuan Yu, Chushih Qi, Xingzhong Ren, Shuzhong Yun, Liaotang Yi, and Muguan Cong—their proclamation of the Dharma-lineage was like a thunderclap or a flash of lightning, such that no one could fathom it. Thereupon, [the Master...]
These great elders were esteemed throughout the world; eminent disciples from the four quarters flocked to them like clouds gathering and mist rising.
They were no different from Hongzhi, Miaoxi, and Zhenxie, who propagated the Way during the Shaoxing era of the Song dynasty. I privately rejoiced, saying:
"In this age of the Dharma’s semblance, how fortunate we are to behold such brilliant radiance of the Buddha-sun and such vast nourishment of the Dharma-rain!"
Within a few decades, the various great elders passed away one after another, leaving the Chan groves desolate and silent, with nothing to be heard.

Even if there were a person or two claiming to be "good friends" (*kalyāṇamitra*), they did nothing but concoct eccentric doctrines and shout out reckless blows to deceive the villagers and women of the lanes; they were truly of the fox species. Thus, those who possess discernment...
He smiled but did not speak. The life-vein of our patriarchs is but a single hair; how lamentable it is!

Among them, there are occasional men of brilliance who remain deeply hidden in the grasses and wilds, refusing to emerge, for they fear that the world would fail to distinguish between the Jing and the Wei rivers, and that pearls and jade would become mixed with tiles and rubble.
Such was my late Master Nanshi: he was fully equipped in both Confucianism and Buddhism, and proficient in both the Chan school and the scriptural teachings.

He possessed transcendent talent and harbored a marvelous and magnificent capacity. When Master Zhongren resided at Yunyan and received the Dharma from the Master, it was like Ciming receiving the Dharma from Huanglong.
Later, when the Master entered the world, he offered the fragrant incense of succession to the Master, thereby not forgetting his origins.
The Master first resided at Pumen in Suzhou, then at Lingyan, and thirdly moved to become the abbot of Wanshou.

Not long after, he retired to live in seclusion above the Wusong River. There, he delighted in daily engaging in "nonsense talk" with mountain hermits and country elders, completely forgetting the ways of the human world.

Upon the accession of our Sacred Emperor, an edict was issued to all Confucians, Buddhists, and Daoists throughout the empire who were profoundly versed in literary meaning, to compile the *Yongle Dadian*. The Monk responded to this call.
By imperial decree he was summoned and returned. He remained in the capital for three years until the transcription of the scriptures was completed.

At that time, the state was holding a Great Repayment-of-Gratitude Assembly (*Bao'en Dazhaihui*), and the Master participated therein. Before long, the abbot of Mount Jing in Hangzhou vacated his post;

the Office of Buddhist Records (*Senglusi*) unanimously recommended that none other than National Teacher Nanshi could fill the vacancy. Thereupon, the Master joyfully set out and ascended Mount Lingxiao.
Ding held a black-lacquered bamboo whisk and, to test those who had come, let out a lion’s roar; all other beasts fell silent and cowered—how much more so a wild fox!
I here rejoice that the Way of the Patriarchs is reviving, like seeing the solitary moon when the clouds part; the fourfold assembly was filled with joy.
His praise was beyond compare. As the Upādhyāya grew old and ill, weary of worldly affairs, he withdrew from his post.

He selected a site to the left of the Jizhao Pagoda and built a thatched hut to dwell in; nevertheless, students seeking instruction continued to arrive in endless succession, crowding one another like the shoulders of oxen and the heels of ants.
His chief disciple, the Elder Baohua Wenmou, recorded the Dharma discourses of the Upādhyāya from four assemblies and compiled them into a collection.
One volume. He brought it to the capital and requested me to compose a preface for its beginning.

I consider that the Venerable Master received the Dharma from Master Xingong, while I studied under Master Yuan’an; both masters were dharma heirs of Chan Master Yuansou Duan. Thus, I and the Venerable Master—
As fellow disciples of the Dharma-gate, I cannot decline the request to write this preface. The Upādhyāya’s name was Wénxiù, with the style name Nánshí.
He presided over four seats of the Dharma, each leaving behind a legacy worthy of admiration; yet these were merely the incidental achievements of the Upādhyāya, and thus they have been omitted here.
Alas! The Dharma discourses spoken by the Upādhyāya were perfectly circular and harmonious, like the spring responding to all things.
No trace of this remains visible. This record should be carved into woodblocks to be passed down to future generations, serving as a model for later students.
Nevertheless, even among those of the same school, none but those who possess the adamantine eye can grasp its essence. This is the preface.

To keep fish trapped in a stagnant pond is merely to labor in vain by churning up the waves. When Gaoteng saw the stupa pole from across the river, he ran straight toward it;

thirty blows to his heels would have been well-deserved. Xuansha broke his toes with a blow of his staff and then said, "Dharma did not come to the Eastern Land, and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven.

Vast and indistinct—what can such a thing accomplish? Tonight, North Mountain shall grant you a narrow path. Studying the Way is like guarding a forbidden city:

by day one wards off the six thieves; by night one remains alert. When the commander-in-chief of the central army can enforce his orders, peace is achieved without moving a blade of grass or striking a single blow.

"One does not decline to carry water or wade through mud. Nevertheless, tell me: who is the commander-in-chief of the central army?

The *nüzhenhua* flower by the seashore where shepherds graze; the "Wangfu" (Waiting-for-Husband) Stone by the Ju Ma River—the stone strikes red.

Ascending the hall at the commencement of the retreat: When the World-Honored One shut his room, he was driven to a clumsy stratagem by his extremity;

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an instance: Once, when the World-Honored One was being offered two *he-huan* (合歡) and *wu-tung* (梧桐) flowers by the Brahmin Kāla, who held them in his left and right hands, the Buddha called out, "O Seer! The Brahmin responded, "Yes. The Buddha said, "Put them down.
The Brahmin then set down the flower in his left hand. The Buddha called out again, "O Seer! Put them down. The Brahmin then set it down... [and so on].
[The Buddha] dropped a flower from his right hand. The Buddha spoke again, saying, "Let it go. The Brahmin said, "World-Honored One, both my hands are now empty;
what more do you command me to let go of? The Buddha said, "I am not commanding you to let go of that flower."
I taught you to let go of the six external objects, the six internal faculties, and the six intermediate consciousnesses all at once;
when there is nowhere left to abandon, that is your place of liberation from birth and death. At these words, the Brahmin realized the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*).

Although the Buddha is the Great Master of the Three Realms, he still fell into the conceptual calculations of consciousness and merit; he deserves twenty blows of the staff. Even though the Brahmin attained realization, [the Buddha’s fault remains].
He has likewise not yet emerged from the quantitative constraints of conceptual consciousness; he deserves twenty blows. Yet, when Beishan delivers such a critique, tell me:
is there fault or no fault? This is like Xiao He establishing the laws.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The World-Honored One taught: 'All sentient beings revolve in birth and death because they do not know the eternally abiding true mind, the nature-pure and luminous essence.

Conceptualizing. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, do not allow yourself idle moments. This is merely the employment of various deluded thoughts;

heaven revolving to the left and earth revolving to the right; the ninety days of a summer retreat; the twelve hours of a day; eating, sleeping, and moving about in a state of ease.

Spontaneous. For a monk such as this, what fault could there be? Nevertheless, if you go from here and someone asks where you spent the summer retreat, you must by no means say it was at North Mountain.

When you arrive in various places, simply present it in this manner.

This is precisely like a diseased eye seeing flowers in the sky. If you say that I have entered parinirvāṇa, you are not my disciple; if you say that I have not entered parinirvāṇa, you likewise are not my disciple.
My illness has reached the vital organs and cannot be cured—not only would worldly physicians fold their hands in helplessness, but even Jīvaka himself could do nothing."
Even the Divine Physician must retreat three stations. I, a distant descendant of the Northern Mountain, shall today treat him for his ailment.
If I cannot cure him, future generations will forever lose their reliance and protection;
if I can cure him, then the body of purple-gold brilliance—lofty, majestic, and resplendent—will manifest everywhere. (He strikes the whisk.)
The willow color is tender like fresh gold; the pear blossoms are fragrant like falling snow.
The donor has prepared this vegetarian meal and congee. Entering the hall: When great functions arise in profusion, every movement must manifest the absolute truth.
Vimalakīrti satisfied thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas with a single bowl of rice; the lay practitioner Ganji served congee, yet Nanquan smashed the congee pot.
Now tell me: is this the great function of manifold activity, or is it not? "If one casually recognizes the face of the east wind, the ten thousand purples and thousands of reds are all spring."

when the bell rings, everyone returns to the hall; when the meal arrives, we all join our palms."

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is like the cool moon shining across the vast sky; there is not a thousand river that does not reflect its image. Like the springtime returning to the great earth, there is not a single blossom to which it does not reach.

In this Jambudvīpa, vocal sounds constitute the Buddha-work. This Great Being’s gateway of perfect penetration demonstrates entry through the faculty of hearing.
Sentient beings listen with their ears, and thus they pursue the objects of sound; the Great Being listens with his eyes, uniquely manifesting the principle of perfect penetration.
When one faculty is perfected and unimpeded, all six faculties are likewise free from obstruction. Both the hearing and the object heard are exhausted; even the nature of hearing cannot be grasped.
Not only is there no suffering to be endured, but there is fundamentally nothing to be saved. Since the nature of hearing cannot be grasped, it is therefore able to hear perpetually.
There would be neither suffering nor rescue; therefore, one should always rescue from suffering. Proclaim this universally to the people of the world:
they should understand it in this way, and will then be able to awaken to perfect penetration, becoming equal to Avalokiteśvara.
With hair bound in a topknot and wearing a hairpin of thornwood, she carries fish out to sell. It is only because of her excessive compassion that she manifests such strange and uncanny forms.

This is precisely the realm of the responsive capacity. How could the realm of those to be saved be separate from wisdom? Wisdom and the realm are eternally interfused. For this reason, he is also called Avalokiteśvara.

All sentient beings are forever freed from suffering, and in a single instant, they suddenly enter samādhi.

When Yuanwu heard the cock crow, he remained as he was, not leaving his station. Not yet knowing the mechanism of the "upward direction," how could he have understood the "final phrase"?
If you wish to become a son of that house, do not fall into its trap. Turn everything over from bottom to top; forge a new way of life.
Leaping and frolicking within the eye of the needle; playing atop the tip of the banner-pole. The Bhagavāns of the three periods of time are all but cataracts in the eye.
Laughing to death Old Bodhidharma! He came from the West to transmit the ancestral meaning.

To the Librarian Yu: "The characters do not form; the eight strokes are not [the truth]. When a single pivot suddenly strikes home, a thousand differences naturally vanish. The universe is within the range of the eye.
Being able to divide them, yet there is no fixed principle for advancing or retreating, rolling up or unfolding. When it is time to act, one acts; when it is time to rest, one rests.
Shifting the Southern Dipper and replacing the Northern Dipper—why trouble the spirit? Tearing asunder the old molds and shattering the mystical barriers—it takes not even a snap of the fingers.
The ocean of three thousand worlds is within a single hair-tip; the billion Mount Sumerus are beneath one's own feet. A-ha-ha! Ra-ra-li! The bright moon.
How can the pure breeze be compared? Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall; Ciming lays his straw sandals across the room.

To the attendant Di, the National Teacher called three times; the attendant responded three times. This so-called "pecking and hatching" mechanism is still considered a sickness of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. When facing it directly—
Severing the ultimate barrier at once, Linji and Deshan come to beg for their lives. This Chan practitioner’s resolve is extraordinary; his natural disposition is moreover pure and vigorous.
Having realized the transmission outside the teachings, every step he takes is uniquely sublime. Not only does he sweep away the flowers of Vulture Peak, he casually shatters the mirror of Caoxi.
Scattering earth and hurling sand, he destroys the heterodox to manifest the orthodox. The conduct of a man of the Way should be thus.
This was settled yesterday, yet today it is not settled.
As for the Dharma Master Shili,
the supernatural powers of Maudgalyāyana, and the divine eye of Aniruddha— the matter of the Patriarchs' ultimate realization— how could they have ever fully comprehended it?
Niaokuo blew on a cloth-hair; Luzu did nothing but face the wall. There was not much suffering in samādhi; from the beginning, it has always been worth recounting.
A lotus blooms in the twelfth month; the sun’s orb rises at midnight. It is inherently beyond deliberation; why need one discuss gain or loss?
With palms joined, he stood before me; transcendent and without peer. The wall-pestle suddenly transformed into a dragon, startling Vimalakīrti to his knees.

Sending forth Can as the *vina* (steward), his realization of the mind was already ultimate, yet he lacked the necessary effort. Striking the gavel with a semblance of authority, how could he have attained it? If one does not understand the compassion of Longmen, [one will fail].
Child! How could Zhuan-an have grasped this news? The "cracking" and "pecking" are not yet the penetrating divine mechanism. Grasses, trees, tiles, and pebbles all radiate brilliance;
the two, three, four, and seven are all shattered in spirit, while the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas possess no complete majesty.

I have never spoken, yet you first attained realization; you are no match for Xiong-feng, who needlessly wrings his nose. From north of the earth to south of heaven, the Great Practice is proclaimed as the colt gallops forth.
It is as if treading upon something turbid.

To the Abbot Ren, he showed the extraordinary matters within the Great Canon of the Teachings; these are constantly manifested in daily practice. One might exhaust one's thoughts and refine one's essence, seeking to emulate them.
Seeking it, one finds a fierce, blazing fire in a floating bubble. How narrow is the place where Mount Jiuzong is seen!
To say that unrolling the scroll illuminates a thousand worlds is merely the idle measuring of Touzi and Yuyan; their "coming forth" and "entering" are not quite right.
Let them wipe everything away from the very beginning—none are permitted to bear the full burden. How could they compare to this? Or perhaps they are one with it? Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra...

By Xian Jutanu. Following the rhyme, a parting verse for Chan Master Miaozang as he travels abroad. Later, upon returning to visit his father and the Reverend Duan’an of Qingshou, [Miaozang] took a step and trod upon the road to Chang’an;
encountering circumstances and meeting conditions, nothing was not wondrous. The warbling of the oriole resounds at Mount Zhong.
Pine trees; herons with joined talons rest upon the grass of the long islet. Red tongues of flame emerge from the southern breeze as the sunflowers bloom in all their loveliness.

Green dots appear on the small lotus leaves of West Lake. Neither the half-character nor the full-character can describe it. Ten thousand *li* of azure sky, the red sun blazes bright. North Mountain speaks thus to uphold the truth:
"Without cause, you have been burdened into a state of incompleteness. If you wish to reach completion, go home and swiftly topple this old Chan monk!"

The attendant Yuanmeng was shown how to serve tea without any pointing or indication. At every house door is the road to Chang’an; before heaven and earth were cleft, one must already turn back the head.
The hawk has already flown past to Silla. The cliffs collapse and the rocks split—the primordial mechanism. Step by step, one directly transcends.
Profound and subtle! Those with yellow heads and blue eyes cannot grasp it; how could those with dragon-like pupils or hawk-like eyes ever fathom it?

To conceal one’s capacity while awaiting the right time—how joyful and liberating! Follow the model of the former patriarchs and do not slacken yourself. With a single clap of thunder, the Dragon Gate resounds;
traverse the ten-thousand-mile journey as you will.

The attendant Songli is utterly naked and starkly bare. As soon as one attempts to take this up, one falls into intellectual understanding. When a single pivot shifts and one looks at the ultimate source, ten thousand bays and a thousand streams all become the vast ocean.
Whether there is existence or non-existence, emptiness or non-emptiness—it is capable of rescuing those in suffering and distress and opening the eyes of the blind.
Deaf! When the Attendant Shan picked up a piece of stone, he startled Chuiyan Zhen Dianxiong into a fall. His upward-pointing function is beyond all comparison;
it transcends past and present, illuminating the entire universe. Rubbing his old eyes atop Beishan, he wishes to behold the Peng bird soaring ninety thousand li.
Sending Attendant Miao to the Capital:
Purity, wisdom, wondrous perfection—fundamentally empty and still from the start. Pervading all of space, it leaves no trace and no mark. The tabby cat and the white ox surely know it;
the Tathāgatas of the three periods do not recognize it at all. The Way-farer’s spirit and resolve are truly extraordinary. Three times he called out his name.
Previously, through a personal recommendation, he attained realization; he held his staff upside down as he ascended Mount Penglai. A whistling, pure breeze arose throughout the eight directions.

He sent off the attendant Zhen, for whom every point is wondrous and every dharma is true. Within the mountains, rivers, and the great earth, not even a speck of dust exists. He has grasped it before the movement of the mind.
He then returned. His hands were so adept that they could communicate with the divine; he could turn heaven and earth upside down without expending any effort.

Capable of benefiting sentient beings and engaging with others, he was fit to occupy the essential ford. He extinguished the orthodox Dharma-eye of Linji, bringing the flowers and trees of Shaolin back to the warmth of spring.

Whether the Abbot Yong comes and goes, or does not come and go; whether he is the treasury or not the treasury—speak it forth from the mouth of faith, and you will naturally be able to reach the truth.
You will directly cause the four sevens and two threes to have their souls flee and their hearts fail in terror, even if it were Deshan or Linji with blows falling like raindrops.
A shout like a thunderclap; as for brandishing oars and dancing with paddles, striking the ground and rolling balls—manifesting a thousand forms and ten thousand states.
A ten-fathom lotus blooms in the midwinter month; a thousand-fathom wave surges from level ground. The man of the Way comes from Qichuan;
how magnificent is his resolve! He never waits to lift a brow; what he has attained transcends all measure. Amidst the wind, he smiles and bids farewell, picking up the crow.
The wisteria vine. Ten thousand miles of heaven and earth, the spring vast and boundless.
Sending off Venerable Fen; Xinghua strikes Kebin. Red earth smeared on a cow’s udder; a fine of money and a meal of rice. A *suōgē* crab with a permanent belly.
A smile at the opportune moment suddenly overturns it all; striking the void to produce sound—how could it be difficult?
A winged tiger laughs amidst the forest groves; a brilliant phoenix soars through the clouds. In the second month of spring in Jiangnan, the season is at its finest;
every thing is direct and straightforward, without any entanglement. When parting before the Chan-Moon Hall, a single yellow oriole sings from the treetop.

Sending off Attendant Puxi, responding on behalf of another: Striking the meditation bench while facing guests—how can a square adze fit a round mortise? This seeker of the Way has not yet entered my chamber;
his vast spirit would seem to scrape the azure heavens. Now that this seeker of the Way has entered my chamber, the clutter within his breast is cleared away.

To be vast and without anything left behind or stored away—yet to go thus is still to involve deliberation. Directly forgetting both subject and object, severing all conceptualization, one naturally finds every step to be extraordinary.
Cutting the rope, the qilin strides upon the celestial shore; unbridling the Lu-er horse, it gallops along the broad highway.
Miaoxi snapped his bamboo whisk in two; Fanhuluo’s single drop of water was sprinkled everywhere across the eight wildernesses.
The forty-seven patriarchs of India and the twenty-three of China—dividing the precarious and spreading the perilous, they merely boast of their linked fragrance.
Seeing off Vinaya Master Jiekong as he returns to Qiantang:

When the Dharma Master first arrived from Qiantang, the green mountains rose majestically as mist and clouds parted. He eloquently expounded the monastic codes and elaborated upon the precepts of observance and violation;

his dialectical skill flowed like the Milky Way, truly a rare talent. Those who came to listen from near and far gathered like a cloud of dust; those with sharp faculties and those with dull capacities were all [enlightened].
His vows have been fulfilled. Exquisite fruits and rare flowers he swiftly gathers; divine incense and ambrosia are offered by non-human beings.

His reputation spreads far and wide, heard across the eight directions; it is as if the Southern Mountain has now been reborn. Out of compassion for this degenerate age, his observance of the precepts is relaxed;
how could he merely love to wander among the people of the world? Now the Dharma Master departs again for Qiantang, carrying a single staff and a single flask wherever he stays. From India...
Visiting old haunts before the peaks: the moon sets over the *śāla* trees at the Su Tai Terrace.
Sending off the attendant monk to Jing Shan—neither relying on words nor departing from them;
one already knows it has become "the second" the moment the mouth opens. When the pivot of the mechanism suddenly turns, one moves toward the ultimate.
Look! There is a pure breeze stirring heaven and earth. When Baizhang first visited Maboji, there were ten thousand bushels of doubt within his breast.
When the tip of his nose was pinched and he suddenly felt the pain, ten billion suns and moons radiated their brilliance. A man who studies the Way should rouse his will;
he should wag his tail straight like a red-tailed carp. With an effortless leap, he passes through the Dragon Gate at the summit of a thousand peaks.
Above, waves arise.
The Qian family, pure and upright, carved the woodblocks for the *Commentary on the Complete Enlightenment Sutra* to offer merit to their parents and requested a preface for its conclusion:
"The Great Ocean of Complete Enlightenment is originally clear and still; Buddhas and sentient beings cannot be apprehended. Mañjuśrī raises waves upon level ground."
Tao: The Bhagavan has not yet escaped becoming a tangled mess. The Tathāgata’s original arising was never caused by conditions; how much more so when one knows there is neither self nor person?
Once the four ailments are departed and the three contemplations have vanished, where in the great trichiliocosm could one seek even a speck of dust? Old Chan Master Guifeng is far too talkative;
he indulges in conceptual discrimination within the non-conceptual, using commentaries to annotate the sutras and sub-commentaries to annotate those commentaries. Blazingly—six...
The moon drifts through frost and snow. Master Pang Yun, the Layman of the Thatched Cottage, once investigated the wondrous meaning of the *Awakening of Faith*.
At the end of his life, his mind remained undisturbed; how carefree he was in passing from birth into death! His daughter’s filial devotion was even more unfathomable:

she commissioned artisans to re-carve the woodblocks for his commentaries on the sutras and treatises, so that they might circulate forever as long as heaven and earth endure, thereby repaying her parents’ virtue and the toil of their nurturing.
The Buddha’s Flower speaks a verse to offer praise; those who slander it sink into the foul, lacking the golden-yellow reputation. All myriad phenomena rise together in dance;
the stone "Shanggan" before the steps laughs itself to pieces.
A Memorial for My Dharma Brother, Venerable Suigan, who Resided at Zunjia Baolin’s Sengmuan Hermitage:
What a display of total mastery and wondrous function! Your tongue turns up waves and billows; your brush brings forth wind and rain.

Your reputation was as close as a shoulder-to-shoulder embrace with [the masters] Song, Zhong, and Ling. Although it has been long since you entered nirvana, throughout the land one still hears the roar of the lion.
The Lion’s Roar. His disciples, numbering in the thousands, widely propagated his teachings throughout the cities and marshlands.

The Master had long relied upon Mount Zhongfu; at the spot where the wooden barrel箍 (gūn) exploded, he attained Zen. He once received the personal seal of approval from my elder brother; among other disciples, who else could have surpassed him?
Furthermore, at Cold Spring, he offered a single silence—how could it be grasped by intellect or measured by consciousness? Fifty.
Throughout the year, the discourse remains incomplete; the "Four Sevens" and "Two Threes" cannot be transmitted. From this point on, the talk falls among the thickets of the monastic community;
the deployment of means is not like that of ordinary times. A fine steed must indeed emerge from the shallow water; a phoenix ultimately encounters the cage.
One’s departure and arrival follow conditions as well as merit. When Yuanwu retired to Shu in his time, it was not for the sake of the glory of Baolin as his native land.

I know that you yourself can surely follow in the footsteps of your predecessors. Now that I am old, I dwell as a guest on the slopes of Fengfu; since you have come to ask for a parting gift, there is nothing more to say.
Dwell in the mountains with care, do not seek fame or profit; you should strive to emulate the character and standards of the ancients.
Next, following the rhyme of Master Quan’an, I show this to Xu Fuyuan:

As soon as one engages in thought, it is no longer the true phrase; how could one permit both hearing with the ears and seeing with the eyes? Since time immemorial, the thousand sages have been unable to transmit it;
laughable indeed is Vimalakīrti’s discourse on non-duality. If you can realize it directly, it will truly suffice; naturally, you shall then reach the state beyond words.
What region? Every head and every object is fully manifest; once this is realized, there is no need for further deliberation.

The nose is straight and the eyes are askance—know this from here. Facing south, one gazes at the North Star. Borrowing the old woman’s shawl, one bows to her on New Year’s Day; riding the thief’s horse, one still pursues the thief.
The Three Essentials and Three Mysteries are all shattered asunder; Linji and Deshan are brought under control by a single stroke. Do not disdain it.
How much more abundant is his spirit! A great man should act in this manner.

Following the original rhyme, I send this verse for Tianjie’s Chan Master Tian as he enters the Cloud Rock Chamber and ascends Fengshan: "The lifelong vow to study the Way is already fulfilled; having been able to bring back the rhinoceros horn,"
Child! When one casually repays a question with silence, the *Mahesvara*’s true eye opens at the crown of the head; mountains, rivers, and the great earth are without a speck of dust.
What division can there be between merging with darkness and merging with light? Let the Hu come and the Han come as they may; I, an old man, have no words for saving others.
The *Chuan Deng Lu* and *Guang Deng Lu* are like white fish gnawing through wood—laughing at that Zhongyi for being so groundless, he stubbornly took a macaque...
The Parable of the Monkey and the Six Windows.
When the Chan master Shenwei was sent to Piling, his resolve was no small matter. Regarding the ultimate barrier of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, he overturned it all with a single laugh.
The Three Mysteries are suddenly rent asunder; the Five Ranks are likewise swept away. Where is Mañjuśrī’s trace? Where can Samantabhadra be sought?
The great earth is silent under the wind; the ten directions are bright with the blazing sun. The wooden band of the bucket falls yet too late; the peach blossoms bloom not too soon.
As you depart from here, you should strive with diligence to greatly revitalize the Way of Shaolin.
The Guest Manager Sengyu read the *Transmission of the Lamp* on a rainy night: "The spirit is exhausted and both fall into ruin; alas, the old man of Longmen sits once more within the coals."
Zen practitioners, take careful note: do not emulate him. To emulate him is ultimately not the mark of a true man. From the beginning, he has held the precious serpent in his own hand;
moreover, the divine talisman hangs from his elbow. Beishan spoke thus without cause; he had already cast his entire body into the wild weeds.
Letting go of the hand, he walks beyond the realm of Aeon-Prime; naturally, a pure breeze comes sweeping in.
Sengxian, the Abbot, speaks of the Tathāgata’s forty-nine years of teaching: it is much like calling a tortoise a turtle.

Since Ānanda first compiled the teachings from the beginning, he has once again stubbornly driven a stake into empty space. The firewood embers have not yet settled; Daobian’s monk’s robe remains entirely as it was.
Torn and worn, with a single breath he turns it slightly better; the *bi-dong* (steamed buns) are even more pitiable. The practitioner’s spirit is exceptionally fierce;

seeking in the east and inquiring in the south, he seeks a definitive resolution. Having personally followed the masters of the monastic groves, how could Beishan (North Mountain) bear to speak further?
The true lineage of Yangqi hangs by a thread; from now on, there will likely be no room for idle dwelling. A thousand feet...
"Take up the long pole with haste; catch the fish that swallows ships in the Eastern Sea.
To the attendant Shilu:
The path above, which not a thousand sages have transmitted, is directly penetrating and lies right before one's eyes; see it clearly."
It can be carried away; the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot block it. It moves spontaneously, turning heaven and earth back to their original state;
its total capacity appears and disappears without hesitation or obstruction. When Yuanwu first saw Dongshan, ten-thousand-fathom iron mountains stood how towering!
Within the sound of Little Jade, his nose was struck off; the golden rooster flew up onto the balustrade and crowed. How extraordinary is this—how extraordinary! The Eye...
When the inner lacks sinews, one is deluded by others; with a wave of the hand, one ascends to the crown of Vairocana. Only then is this the good news from the West.
As for the attendant Seseng, the *qin*, *se*, and *konghou* possess wondrous sounds, yet without wondrous fingers, they cannot be made to resonate. Sentient beings fundamentally abide as Tathāgatas.
Family. Without meeting a true guide, one will ultimately never reach the goal. This is why Yuanwu studied under Dongshan; he moved through his training without ever shrinking from hardship.
When the rooster crowed once, his eyes were opened; with a flick of his arm, he passed straight through a thousand gates.
His skillful use of the tongs and hammer to forge Buddhas and patriarchs was truly illuminating. The wind-chasing wooden horse neighs atop the mountain; the stone child holds its infant.

The woman laughed by the stream: "A man of the Way has come from afar, from the City of Clouds. Serving at my side with exceptional devotion—whether it be me who bears you or you who bear me, let us not discuss it.
We shall see you soar upon the ten-thousand-li journey of the Peng bird."
In praise of the Abbot Xingzang (whose taboo name was Zixing, a native of Jianchang Prefecture):
That one pivotal point regarding his parents' life before birth—before he even left Ganjiang, it was already settled. Entering the gate, he shook his staff and circled the meditation seat;

though free from illness, he stubbornly demanded medicine. Jingshan’s way of providing such guidance is like using yellow leaves to stop a child’s whimpering. It is but a vain attempt to quell delusion.
The child cries; the True Eye at the crown of the head is as bright as the sun. Shaking his head, he returns home as a fine steed gallops away.
The autumn mountains are azure and the autumn waters are green. One phrase, clearly realized, transcends ten billion worlds. A woman with蛾眉 (yúméi) brows has a long beard;
the Śūnyatā-deva’s face is crimson.
A gift for Preceptor Cong:
The Tathāgatagarbha has seven openings and eight apertures; it has always resided upon the tip of a single hair.
If you see it clearly and recognize it intimately, in the end it remains not truly real. Dongshan spoke of *praṇidhāna*; with a mere staff, he firmly grasps the void.
Regarding the measure of emptiness: Yunmen cast down a faggot of firewood; amidst the blazing flames, he flew with pure frost. "In my school, there is no dharma and no phrases;
I am too weary even to raise the bamboo staff toward others. All day long he sits motionless, his mouth agape like a *lú-dū* bird;
who asks whether he betrays me or betrays you? This seeker of the Way comes from the banks of Jinquan; the vast qi within his breast swallows the rainbows and halos. He circles the meditation seat...
Circumambulating three times, he stands out prominently. Mount Jing does not trouble itself to raise an eyebrow; the lamp-stand and the lantern bow their heads in unison.
The wind blows the stone mortar as it runs through the air. A single stroke completely transcends all kalpas past; Śākyamuni did not exist after Dīpaṃkara.

To the Head Librarian Xue, he showed that both the Great Canon and the Small Canon must be cast aside. When one can manifest and enter [the Way], what question remains? A single pivot is revealed at the head of a thousand sages;
in curing illness, why rely on medicine carried by a donkey? He laughs at Master De’s mouth opening in vain; the paper for wiping sores follows from this.
Where does it come from? Old Shaoyang with his lame feet lacks agility; even when answering a single question, he merely wanders about in circles.

Fortunately, there was Dongshan who was slightly more capable; after all, how could he ever allow for deliberation? When Yangdao uttered "Pralāṇa," the bright moon and clear breeze spread forth without end.
How many complications have been swept away! Xiong峰 facing the wall lost out to the old barbarian. If you reach...
Passing through the gate of Jingshan, do you realize that you are still halfway there? The Way-farer has his own extraordinary stratagem;
he refuses to fall into the snares of others. Without storing a single grain of rice or a stalk of vegetable, he cuts off the vital thoroughfare to receive the clouds and waters.
I escort the Lord of the Earth, along with earth, water, fire, wind, space, awakening, and consciousness, throughout the entire realm of sand-grains, leaving no trace behind.

This single pearl within the Tathāgata-garbha has been personally retrieved once the paper robe was cast off. When the dark moon vanishes, the bright moon appears; its light illuminates both past and present.
Yaoxuan: "The white ox and the stray cat understand how to nod their heads; the Tathāgatas of the three periods have not realized it at all. A follower of the Way came from my own hometown yesterday;
swallowing the rainbows and halos in his breast, how magnificent he is! With one twist of his bamboo staff, he breaks it into two pieces;
with a single gulp from the bowl-basin, he sucks dry the rising dust. As the autumn wind rustles through the tall trees, he suddenly departs, piercing the clouds with his staff. On another day..."
Before others, he acts with reckless blindness. A five-colored auspicious qilin strides upon the celestial shore.
Chan Master Shichun came to Gusu in his youth; he once attended Fuhua on North Mountain. Before the pivot of action, he never waited for the third strike.
"Ha! All Buddhas are suddenly empty, with no self. A bundle of firewood flies down from the peak of Zhongfu. What transcendent is this divine mechanism, appearing and disappearing?
A swift falcon soars across the azure heavens; a noble steed gallops through the rising smoke. We shall meet again atop Mount Lingxiao;
what need is there to discuss the 'Sun Face' or the 'Moon Face'? In a bright window, a single mat has grass for its cushion; for food, there is yellow rice."
Among the grains and vegetables there is amaranth; one must recognize that its flavor is long-lasting within its plainness. Contemplate well the Divine Cauldron and Fachang;

though they boasted of their thatched huts and earthen-jar wine, how could they have possessed thousands of granaries or ten thousand chests? I am ashamed that I cannot yet practice the Way of the Ancients, yet I rely on you to harmonize with this refined excellence.
Together we shall support the lineage of Jibei, so that for a thousand ages the pure wind shall spread ever more vast.
Sometimes he brandishes his black bamboo staff; with the eye of Maheśvara, who could possibly peer into it? In the flash of lightning, he suddenly snatches it away;
on a mountain peak in years to come, he will act as he pleases.
Next, following the rhyme of my elder brother, the Venerable Huancheng, I show Layman Zhou Daoxiang that the True Buddha has no form.
The Great Way is originally without direction; that which can be seen and that which can be reached are known to be not auspicious.
Dongping vainly claims he can practice goodness; Simiao merely boasts of transcribing Buddhist scriptures.

If you have not yet clarified that one crucial point, in the end, you will all simply be turning along with external objects. For now, do not ask how it is; let go, and it happens in a single instant.
To revolve the pivot of heaven and turn the axis of earth—all this depends on me, not on another.
When the Chan master Huì was shown that he had not yet left Bǎishān Temple, he had already entered the Buddha-flower chamber at Jìngshān;
yet when he came to burn incense and offer greetings, his nostrils were plucked while his eyes were lost. When Déqiáo bumped into Lóngtán, Lóngtán simply held up a piece of paper.
Blowing out the candle: a single white staff becomes a wooden boot. Lightning crashes, rain pours, and thunder flies.
Be careful not to learn such a trick; to catch the sound and receive the void turns it into error. Overturning the old tracks, he unfurls a new branch;
across the vast, empty sky, a solitary eagle soars.

In the summer of the Renzi year of the Hongwu era, I resided at Tiger Hill (Hǔqīu). While recording the various famous sites within the mountains, all [my associates] offered congratulations in verse.
I have thus composed this one poem in response.
A single smile before the surging peaks of the sea; when the occasion arises, face-to-face, there is no deception. Yangshan’s spiritual powers were wondrous within his dreams;
Jicui’s refined thoughts were vast within his breast. Grasping the cloth-hair to clarify essence and function, he overturned the ocean of the Tripitaka until all waves ceased.
How many men with eyes of iron and copper—none can harmonize with this one song of springtime.

On the occasion of the Longevity Celebration, Master Zhongdao Xingzang entered the Hall of Joyful Radiance (*Xiyi-shi*). The myriad layers of the Flower Treasury (*Huazang*) were all overturned at once;

beneath the tips of the hundred grasses, the Patriarch’s intent was clarified, and upon the tip of a single hair, the source was recognized. Longtan blew out Deshan’s candle, and Liangsui pushed open Mazu’s door.
The valley gates: the liver and gallbladder are both casually rent asunder. A gnat swallows Mount Kunlun of iron.
Upon sending off a monk who has returned to Huating after receiving the precepts:
when the mind is absent, there are neither precepts nor mind. On level ground, cease planting forests of thorns. When the understanding of dharmas does not persist, dust naturally subsides.

Exhausted! As soon as deluded sentiments stir, karma deepens again. In the fourth dhyāna, there is ultimately neither formation nor destruction; throughout the ten ages, when has there ever been past or present?
Suppressing his majestic radiance, he spoke once more: "The boatman of Zhu Jing is one who knows this."
To My Dharma Brother at Duku Hermitage, also presented to Master Xilu:
Who else is there who has cut off the world? In the depths of the sea-clouds, you find your rest. Those with copper heads and iron jaws die before a word is spoken;
Those with hawk-eyes and dragon-pupils are lost beneath a shout. The path is opened wide to distinguish inner and outer; The secure barrier is firmly held, leaving no passage.
A hair’s breadth. There is another true message beyond that; it is permitted only for the members of the same household, father and son, to know.

Resting within the chamber of Fo-rong, the Dharma Master’s banner of victory stands high as the various māras are crushed. The white ox and the tabby cat exclaim, "How excellent! Under the moon's orb on this auspicious night, all darkness [is dispelled].

Extinction: the central pillar amidst the currents, where the hundred rivers turn back. The principles of the Supreme Vehicle’s Chan are now fully elucidated; the comprehensive discourses of the nine assemblies have already been annotated.
Surely the youth who has traveled south must arrive; I pray that the gate of the Chan pointers may be opened for him to hear.
The Abbot Sengnian sees his mother off at Tingpu;
after the rain, green sprouts emerge. For a compassionate mother, her hair has turned white with the passing years.

It was fitting for one who has left the household life to sever worldly attachments, yet how can she help but feel sorrow upon encountering this scene? Why must he carry firewood like Lu Jiaolao? Why need he labor to mend shoes like [the artisan]?
Muzhou: "Casting off my hands, I have arrived home with nothing to offer; the debt of your labor and kindness is repaid all at once.
I congratulate Master Huguan upon his residence at Beichan.

Having long cultivated the power of vows and mastered extensive learning, you awakened early to the gates of Tiantai contemplation and practice. You wield the axe atop the heads of the thousand sages.
Carving out the world upon a single hair-tip; at Mount Xing, dung-fire roasts the yellow tubers. In the golden palace, tea bowls are set before the Sovereign.
On this day, Beichan opens his Dharma seat; surely the dragons and elephants of the four seas will hasten there.
Sent by the Venerable Fuku to rejoin Master Tianquan Shi;

after the man of the Way fought the dragon-river of the Dharma, taking and giving according to the occasion was entirely his own freedom. How could a fierce tiger ever eat the flesh of those it has subdued?
Why must a divine immortal wait for a noble title? The sun and moon hang freely across the realm; the heroes beyond the passes let out their roars.
Tashou then laughed at Master Ma’s single shout, saying, "Pointlessly peddling Yangzhou inside one's own house.
Next, he composed verses in the style of Master Yan Lanjiang to see off Xia Zhenyin as he returned east:
"When a single thought arises, a Buddha is perfected; The sands of afflictions are cast away with ease. Every single thing is entirely Vairocana."

The Treasuries—wherever they may be—are all cities of Ultimate Bliss. Having swept away the five periods and the five flavors, and cleared away the three types of wisdom and the three insights, he raises the "Song of Returning Home" before the wind; with bamboo staff and straw sandals, listen attentively!
In the same rhyme, I respond to the former Abbot Yuzhong of Kaiyuan, who has spread a single mat within this ancient Chan palace. Your lofty character transcends the Five-Crested Peak;

when you raise your staff, all intellectual devices are lost, and as soon as your gāthā emerges, all meanings are empty. You are a vessel for travelers long lost in the sea of suffering, a bellows for the Caoxi tradition.
The lineage has fallen; Zen does not reside in discursive thought—this is a sickness. With such a long tongue, one ought to laugh at Old Huanglong.
Entrusting [the Dharma] to Xian at Tianning, he revealed his own snow-like mind;
he himself had great affinity with Bilin. The gate of transmission was reopened to demonstrate the single transmission; the story of the Go-board Stone resounds through the heavens.
On this earth, the people of Mleccha cast off their veils and entanglements; the blazing red sun dispels the darkness, and the heroic great general occupies the central stronghold.
The public case of the former master is resolved at that very moment—what need is there to wait twenty or thirty years?
Borrowing the rhyme of Venerable Quanshi, I lament Venerable Huayan Yingzhong:
He was clearly seen, without a single flaw; Only his own brothers could truly know him.
When traveling together on the mountain paths, When sharing a smile within the Water-and-Bamboo Pavilion— Not only did the clay ox shed sweat, But even the stone woman was moved to tears.
My heart is filled with sorrow. Do not say that these words have no one to whom they may be entrusted. The myriad phenomena and all living beings understand how to uphold them;
they understand without partiality and act without deficiency. They are worthy of being specially perceived and known by the Worthy King.

When the Way was first established as the guiding principle, and when Zhu’an stayed three nights in the Meditation Hall, the profound wind began to stir and the dragons and phoenixes rejoiced; yet the Buddha-sun suddenly declined amidst the weeds.
How sorrowful! In Great Samādhi, there is originally no mark of arising or ceasing. The moral cord has fallen; who will uphold it now?
In the same rhyme, I send this to Zhensong Shi of Mount Ding:
In the eighth month, autumn is high and the moon fills the void. With whom can the message from the West be communicated? The snake arises upon the rope, yet it is because of...

Consciousness: The banner moves at the tip of the pole; it is not the wind. When subject and object, measure and known are forgotten, knowledge and views vanish. Beyond the subtle and the minute, the root is ultimate and right and wrong are merged.
Sitting in meditation amidst the pines upon a steady rush-mat—truly, this transcendence is rarely shared by those in the world.
Revealing clearly, he empties his own kalpa; traveling through Liang and traversing Wei, he sought to circulate [the Dharma]. With a divine bow, he can shatter a thousand layers of armor;
with the wings of a great鹏 (peng) bird, he can strike the winds of ten thousand li. When objects do not arise, the mind does not arise;
where principle is perfectly fused, phenomena are perfectly fused. To the descendants of Jibei, he yields his hand; holding it sideways or using it upside down, he is unlike anyone else.
To Master Yizhou (who had retired from Tianning and returned to Puzhao):
How leisurely is the coming and going of this old Chan master! It is simply because he has always possessed "One Boat. When ascending, he must cause one to descend;
though he enters the stream, he never consents to flow with it. Master Huo’s willow-oar presents its dance; Old Cheng casts his fishing line.
Again gathered in; how joyful that all sentient beings are now fully delivered. They return once more to moor at the ancient sandbar.
The Yuebo Pavilion (Moon-Wave Pavilion) is so named because it faces the lake; when the moon comes, why wait for the hour of deep night? Stirred by the ripples yet not dispersing—this is not for...

Exquisite! Piercing through water without leaving a trace is not yet marvelous; Touzi’s response to the monk was exceptionally penetrating, while Nanquan’s waving of his sleeves gave rise to suspicion.
Only when both light and object have utterly vanished can one’s words truly accord with those of Caoxi.

Jingxin Yuan has been sent to Chong’en to take up his official appointment and return east as its abbot. When the plum blossoms are half-ripened in the river city, if he can open the gate of the single transmission, the elegant tradition of successive generations may be pursued once more.
He brings forth Yangshan’s "dry dung pellet" and overturns Jizhao’s almsbowl.
The Basin Pond. To those who study the profound mystery upon the sea, let them know that the Xi family has such a son.
In the same rhyme, I respond to Master Wuan of Baoben, whose double locks have turned white as he faces the twilight years:
"With a broad smile, he tosses back his pillow and rises amidst the shade of the vines. Though the cords of the school’s纲 (guiding principles) may be loosened, it is not [the end]."
In the past, when the sun of the Buddha turned its light back upon this very moment, the waters swelled and the boat naturally floated; even the fermented vinegar still has flies vying to find it.
This single board of a chess-stone from our patriarchs—how could its value be less than ten thousand pieces of gold?
Using Rhymes to Show My Parting from Layman Hai Tongfuzong: The gate of Shaoshi has not been visited together;
To recognize the earthenware is mostly a mistake regarding the shadows. Casually treading upon it, one realizes it is not the self;
This wondrous discourse has reached from antiquity to the present. Where words are spoken, the faculty of the mind-mind must be severed; When awakening occurs, how can dream-visions remain?
They can only seek out; the wild fox clan merely forms a troop. A one-horned qilin naturally excretes gold.

I have taken refuge at Mount Jing, paying respects to the Venerable Zhong, with whom I formerly shared an invitation to enter the Imperial Capital. How could a qíjì (stallion) and a nútái (lazy horse) share the same road? My dharma-practice has become like a huángyáng (holly oak)—meeting only with setbacks.

In this intercalary year, the divine strategist and haughty general have obtained the numinous talisman; they habitually employ the carp from the mountain peaks for the sake of men. I, an old man, can do nothing but watch the crows upon the roof.
I hear that the tally-sticks in the chamber are nearly full, yet how can I bear it when the talented and brilliant are still rushing forward?

Among the famous mountains under heaven, there is Mount Wujie. Humbly receiving the Imperial mandate, I propagate the True Doctrine. The decree of my title as "National First" (Guoyi) was bestowed with profound grace;
tea and cleansing extend harmony, and the Way flourishes alongside. Do not bring up the dust and weeds at the bottom of the well; the bamboo shoots of the Southern Mountain are fit for circulation.
Piercing through buildings and spanning over stoves are but trivial matters; I take supreme joy in sharing from afar the breeze beneath the moon.

Entrusting this to Master Weian of Songyin, questions regarding the Dharma were answered with a cough and a spittle; the ancestral Way of the Southeast has become increasingly flourishing. Is it not that once the seal is cast, it is immediately melted down?

It must be that having looked at the tower, one then strikes the tower. Within the snap of a finger, the forty-two gates [of meditation] are realized; the hundreds of thousands of samādhis are attained in a single moment.
Regarding the "tip of a hair," the practitioners of various quarters all treat it as mere child's play; they do not resemble this elder rolling a brocade ball.

He lamented that his Dharma brother, the late Venerable Su’ān of Linggu, had attained the true transmission of the wondrously luminous mind-seal. For ten years in the Imperial Capital, he manifested the power of transformation; in striking the tiger, he did not employ three [blows].

With a mere cubit of staff, he casts down the single coil that once caught the giant turtle; the whirlwind is suddenly stilled by the cool shade of his tree, and the bitter sea is instantly overturned by the Prajñā boat.
The monastic groves lie desolate as the autumn day grows cold; who now shall play the lute of the *gongu* for this rare melody?
Respectfully addressed to Master Yezhou of the Eastern Hall at Jitian Temple: I seek a title for the *Biography of Layman Yuanyan*.

His appearance is like a soaring rock or a flashing lightning bolt, containing the essence of frost. He is the primal tortoise of the Great Dharma and the pillar of the Buddha’s regulations. Whether bowing or rising, whether moving or turning, he is entirely the Patriarch.

In thought, jesting and scolding are both the expression of the Way; as Zhaozhou grew old, his spiritual mechanism became even more rigorous. As the celestial omen was transmitted, the Dao flourished ever further.
The great gate of giving is opened without obstruction; the ancestors still await the manifestation of their hidden radiance.
In the same rhyme, I respond to the Venerable Master Mìyìn Zōng of Tiānfēng on Mount Zhōngfù:

"Upon the head of the mountain, where the sea-surging peaks rise, How many times have we shared a single mat to discuss the ancestral school? Its vast capacity and subtle function are difficult to fathom;

Through generations of true transmission, its prosperity has been maintained. The road turns through a thousand bends as one enters alone on horseback; A pearl passes through nine curves in a single string."
The silk threads are connected. At Yan’ou’s Snowy Peak and Ao-shan’s Inn, one must raise the white flag of surrender to the wind below.

As the Rectifier of Affairs Zheng sends it forth, he lifts up the golden hammer, shining bright as the sun; the courage and souls of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are startled. The divine fish will surely follow the spring thunder.
Go! How could a colorful phoenix ever be ensnared by an iron net? At the tip of Xinghua’s staff, a heavy punishment was meted out; atop Cuiyan’s hall, they welcomed him with a smile.
Without needing a cough, everything was cast aside; beyond the clouds, a range of green mountains stretches across the horizon.

I reveal to Master Xing a matter from before the empty kalpa: Clearly and brightly, all moving and still things proclaim it together. A multicolored wild goose strikes the Milky Way, casting its shadow across autumn;
The crimson cassia holds the breeze, exhaling its evening fragrance. One surely knows that even the Great Canon cannot fully explain it; Even the Patriarchs were still mistaken.
On Discernment: The wheel of mechanism turns within the breast of the man of the Way; he has a unique method for transforming the rotten into the marvelous.
In the same rhyme, I respond to the former Abbot Xingyuan of Chongsheng, Monk Yu, the Scribe, and Attendant Xizang:
Laughing at parting from ordinary people, they cast away the mountain; like soaring wild cranes, they return from the east. Who can fathom this total function of wondrous utility?
Mei: "What kind of lofty wind is this? Who dares to climb it? Qingxi needlessly divided the Canon into eight; Huanglong established three barriers out of nowhere.
Alas, I am old and cannot forget the world; rushing through the dust and toil, I feel deeply ashamed."
Master Ji, the Librarian, spoke of Dongshan’s “A *Bharaṇī*”: “The radiant sun casts its brilliance across the ten directions; Both the provisional and the ultimate teachings fall utterly short.
How could the five ranks of ruler and subject ever correspond? Before the pivot, the myriad paths are cut off; Behind the crown, the light eternally shines upon the ten thousand things.”
A single realization of inner radiance can further transcend the patriarchs; the fragrance of the flower is sensed upon the branches of the papaya tree.

Sending off the Head Seat Ming to Hangzhou, one finds the path home amidst the sound of the Xiao-yu flute. Turning over the ocean of the Tripitaka, he reveals the total upholding; without employing a single shout, he distinguishes guest from host.

Master, you transcend all worldly conditions, severing both awakening and delusion. The vermilion phoenix must surely soar through the azure heavens; how could the azure dragon deign to be trapped in the mire?
On the road by West Lake at the hand of Xi Zi, the spring breeze blows as pairs of white birds fly across the willow embankment.
Sending off Zewei, one call of "Buddha," one strike of the mallet—this is precisely the moment when empty space shatters to pieces. The lamp-stand and the lantern dance together;
the wooden man and the stone woman both lift their brows. Even with wisdom like that of Śāriputra, it would be difficult to fathom; even with eloquence like that of Subhūti, it would be in vain.
Reflecting on this, I shall see you off without the need for further detailed instructions. The autumn wind whistles and the millet stalks sway;

the karmic connection between Master and disciple that has brought us together, O Venerable Vinaya Master Shengsong, is surely no light matter. How could it be compared to ordinary worldly sentiments? It is not that Kebin’s mind is [otherwise].

"Agreed. You surely know that Xinghua’s command was for his disciples to walk on foot; only then would the beard beneath the stone man's chin emerge, and only then would the fruit upon the branches of the iron tree form.
Since I have already entered the mud and further entered the water, you, O *ācārya*, must ensure your Dharma-eye is clear."

Sent off, Venerable Ji, you who once waged a Dharma-battle within the field of selecting Buddhas; without the need for a single shout, you settled the boundaries of the realm. The fires of war across the ten thousand regions have all been extinguished, and the demonic armies of the six aggregates have fled into hiding.
To clarify the fundamental source to its depths is still but the second stage; to see one's nature by penetrating the peak is likewise so.
Ordinary indeed! Though the dragon-sword has not yet emerged from its case in Fengcheng, its cold radiance already pierces the vicinity of the Dipper.

I send this seed of a papaya from Xuanzhou to the *karmadāna* Maowei; may its reflected shadows and continuous brilliance pervade the eight wildernesses, such that the emerald peach within the cavern can hardly compare.

Lush! Within the moon, the vermilion cassias share their fragrance; by the rains of Mount Shou, the roots must surely thrive. With the pure breezes of Kunlun, the flowers have already perfumed the air.
Let us wait for him to become a great vessel in years to come, providing shade and coolness to the monastic groves for a thousand ages.

When Shibo saw the bucket-rim of the *weina* fall to the ground, he immediately knew where it was headed; yet this was not yet the moment of letting go over the precipice. When words penetrate the double mystery, one still involves oneself in intellectual understanding;
when the mind is empty of the myriad dharmas, suspicion still remains. Upon the Ruoshui River the duckweed flowers are white; before the slanting Jade Peak stands the wood...
Ye Fei: What need is there for many annotations on the Northern School? When the occasion arises, there is neither compliance nor opposition.

This demonstrates that Layman Liaoquan has fully realized the nature and is further perfecting his cultivation. The meaning of the Patriarchs is clear at the tips of the hundred grasses; how could there be anything to attain when it is already so?

Attained! What was unfit for excellence has, in turn, become excellent. His two eyes shine brightly, suspended between heaven and earth; ten thousand realms swirl in profusion, freely offering and responding.
Having swept past Hengyang, the old man Pang Yun carries his purse at his waist and rides a crane up to Yangzhou.

Having sent the *karmadāna* to the North Mountain where the assembly is vast, the guiding principles are already established. One must know this for oneself from the source of one's own spirit; it is not like the Buddha being displayed within the hall.
It is precisely like the moment the mallet is struck in the main sanctuary: when the wooden band falls, it is inherently not "wondrous," and for a pillar to sprout flowers is likewise not so.
This is extraordinary: sweeping away two or three, and adding four or seven. The waves of Lake Dongting ripple like azure lapis lazuli.
Responding in rhyme to the one from Mount Dian, Renmoan:
eastward he strikes, and moreover, westward he beats the drum. This is Yunyan’s true heir; his style is peerless, silencing the lion’s lute for all.
How could this resonance be compared to a frog’s stride through mud? Amidst the blazing heavens, a profusion of snow falls; in the twelfth month, a riot of flowers suddenly blooms.
An old man dwelling in the mountains has no other strategy: for many years, a single almsbowl has been his way of life.

Venerable Huàn, you have never raised [the staff] to demonstrate your realization; yet as you encounter objects, you manifest your original radiance at all times. The green waters and blue mountains are not stained by pigment;
the cawing of crows and the chirping of magpies—how could these be ordinary? Yet I pity Dèqiáo for his ability to burn incense and read scriptures, and I laugh deeply at Yúnfēng’s affairs.
Transforming grain; providing rafts for the four modes of birth, one restores the lineage of the patriarchs. When the time arrives, the principle will naturally manifest.

To the attendant who was shown milk, the attendant replied, "I have attained Zen. You must know that there is still a further shore beyond; there is calling and responding, casting oneself into the cage.
Birds: the entire realm and the whole mind are caught in the net of scales. Gold from the ore still awaits smelting; milk is not yet true until it is within the city.
The Buddha-flower is old and weary of distress; the clouds gather over Sutai, and the moonlight is fresh.
Seeing off Abbot Ji as he returns to Chongming:
casually brushing aside the "cloth-hair" kōan, the golden sun flies from the bottom of the sea at midnight. Writing characters in empty space is entirely delusion;
turning one’s body to face a guest is likewise a mistake. Sagehood and worldliness, delusion and awakening—these are but cataracts in the void; mist, dew, clouds, and mists are their very substance.
The upper robe; the boat has already reached the house where the tide rises at Sapu. Chrysanthemum fragrance mingles with the scent of incense filling the forest gate.
Sending this letter to the Abbot Zangzhu of Wulin:
with feet following wherever they may roam, one kicks over the ocean of Huazang; at midnight in Fusang, the sun’s orb is red. The lion that turns its body has never been [bound].

The Secret Instruction: Where could the tracks of the antelope suspended in the air be found? Suddenly restoring the true regulations and original models, I have swept away secret realizations and hidden communications.
If old friends from Wulin were to meet me now, They would find that for the sake of the Way, my two ears have been deaf for years.

Sent to Attendant Dun: One listen to the rooster flapping its wings and crying. Within the breast, there is neither awakening nor delusion; ordinary sentiments and sagely understandings have both vanished.
What use is there for wondrous principles or profound words? Bodhidharma needlessly troubled his journey to China; Yongjia came in vain of his own accord.
Caoxi: From here to the imperial capital, the spring scenery is fine; the willow branches there grow long, level with the surface of the water.
Following the rhyme of Ping’an at Guangxiao, I present this to Chan Master Yan of Jingshan:

He is truly one who breaks through the tower and leaps over the hearth; his conduct and concealment, his speech and silence, are all profound mysteries. His alms-bowl bag has long been with him from Mount Zhong.
Attached: This monk’s staff now returns from Jingwu. The Great Dharma has its source; you have the power to seek it out. Your fragrant name shall fly ever higher without wings.
With compassionate vows to deliver sentient beings and a will to support the school, may you never, even for a moment, depart from this path.

To the attendant Zhan, he showed that at the head of a thousand sages there is a single pivot; when grasped directly in the light, it is utterly free from subtlety. A swift falcon sheds its leather hood and soars toward the heavens;

a horned tiger sprouts wings and flies. To call out three times and receive three responses still involves intellectual understanding; even "the whole mind is the Buddha" has not yet reached the point.
Forget the basis; try to look at the place where it is used upside down and held crosswise—there, even the wrathful Nanda loses his majesty.

To Master Jiàn: the mind-mirror is perfectly bright, penetrating the ten voids; the clouds of the central sky have cleared, and the lunar disc stands solitary. The numinous light blazes, illuminating the present.

Ancient and wondrous, its essence is suchness, transcending existence and non-existence. The five teachings and three vehicles are but mere elaborations; the direct pointing of the single transmission is but a forced designation.
A wooden man claps his hands, a clay ox dances—startling the blue-eyed barbarian who came from the West.

Shixian the Rector proclaims this great causal nexus of Shaolin; let it be widely proclaimed in every object and at every turn. Beyond the window, the yellow oriole is just warbling among the bamboos;
by the stream, the green willows are still holding their mist. Cuiyan has a plan and troubles himself to prepare charcoal; Xinghua, for no reason, desires—
A fine of money. Cutting off both the bright and dark paths. The Jambu tree is on the southern edge of the sea.
Although the Venerable Shidan used the power of layered wondrous mysteries to search for it, in the end, it was all a waste of effort. A single word can cause the ordinary to be liberated.
The Sage: A pill of medicine can transform iron into gold; the wondrous style of the Joyful Land (Abhirati) has no fixed point of reference. The Buddha-work of Jambudvīpa resides in sound;
every dharma before one’s eyes is without concealment. The oriole sings among the green peach blossoms as spring reaches its depths.

Revealing the message from beyond the realm of Kaiwei and Weiyin, it is clearly manifest right now. If you wish to discern whether there is still a thorn within the mud, you must know that fundamentally there is no mind outside the Dharma.
Supporting heaven and propping up earth—how extraordinary! To brush aside the weeds and gaze at the wind is in vain.
While searching for it, he realized its loss only upon seeing the fallen hoop of a wooden bucket: "The warbling oriole has already passed through the green willow shade.

He mournfully showed this to Guang and Zhen at Zhizan, where he had lived in high seclusion for ten years. Throughout his life, he never hesitated to proclaim the teachings widely, overturning the patriarchs and Buddhas to reveal the profound mystery.

Along the road, he cleared away the thorns and brambles to transform it into a jeweled monastery; the morning horn startled the lingering dreams of the槐 (huái) kingdom. The whirlwind blew down the tangled vines and stumps;
though the white clouds of former times are cherished by all, it is only those of my own school who sigh in sorrow.
Farewell to Venerable Hongwei (Dharma-heir of Fahua Temple):
The direct pointing and single transmission have no giver or receiver. The seven parables and three turnings of the Lotus Sūtra— Are neither provisional nor ultimately real.
There is release, yet there must also be gathering. Rolling the wooden ball in the room, he pities Xueqiao; Hanging the fly-whisk from his bed, he laughs at [his own state].

In Hongzhou, such a community has no need for formal entry; like grass bowing before the wind, they move with spontaneous freedom. Following the original rhyme, I congratulate Chan Master Xiangchu of Wanshou Temple on his early arrival from the Prince’s residence to seal his mind.
He has long been accustomed to opening his stall at the Zaojiao and Dengxin markets; his wondrous functioning is like a flash of lightning followed by a clap of thunder.
Shooting: The profound discourse rolls like jade and turns like pearls; it dries up the West River at the very bottom of one's gaze and delicately smoothes the mounting platform before the steps.
When such a critical phrase is raised once more, the stone man laughs, revealing half his cheek.
In Memoriam of Lü Jingfu (who studied the *Avataṃsaka* and recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*):

His learning was vast and his talent eminent; his virtuous conduct was lofty. In his practice of Chan, he surpassed even Master Pang. Within the tip of a single hair, the ten mysteries and six characteristics are present;

within a single thought-moment, the seven parables and three turnings unfold. How could there be any signs of birth, extinction, departure, or arrival? The distinction between sage and ordinary, delusion and awakening, is fundamentally... [non-existent].
No trace remains. I have come alone to offer my condolences after the ten-day mourning period has ended. The tide fills the cold pond; the moon fills the sky.
Next, following the initial rhyme of "Ten Thousand Years of Longevity": To see off Master Min, the Librarian:
He breaks through that one critical barrier before the mechanism moves. Turning heaven and earth is no difficulty for him. He teaches directly so that even the grass he grasps becomes [the Way].
Medicine! Why push the waves to further aid the surging tide? The mountains above the lake stand like jade tables; the moon over the sea-gate rises like a shimmering silver platter.
Within forty-odd years, Gautama stubbornly sought to entrust it all to the tip of his tongue.
This *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* written in blood was inscribed for Hu Juexing.
The meaning of the *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-śūraṅgama* is exceedingly profound; every word strikes like jade and rings like metal. The Tathāgata expounded upon *samādhi*;
the Bodhisattvas cultivated and perfected a forest of myriad practices. When seeing is not seeing, it is called right seeing; where the mind is not the mind, that is the [true state].
True Mind: A single drop of mother-born blood from the tip of a finger; its outflow can surpass all that has come before and after.

*Showing to Layman Xie Xuankui while Sitting at Night:* Frequent night rains have caused me to light cypress seeds; I overturn the layered subtleties and profound mysteries. The great trichiliocosm rests upon the tip of a hair.
Above: The Gate of Non-duality opens before kalpas of eternity. When Lingyun excavated the pond, the hound chased the clod; when Tongxuan composed his treatise, the ants sought the scent of the meat.
In profound stillness, he sits decisively beyond the reach of words and thought; the bell of the sea temple echoes across the shore.

Sent to Master Dizang: The Precious Treasury is Perfectly Accomplished; from the very beginning, kalpas have been empty. The essence of sentient beings and all Buddhas is fundamentally the same. Its attainment does not depend on the power of external conditioning;
its manifestation is not due to the labor of instruction. When Luopo set down his letter, the tortoise dragged its tail; when Deshan burned his commentary, the bird flew away.
Casting it into the cage, he suddenly opens the *kapāla* to reveal the Vajra-eye: the pupils of the ocean shore shimmer as the morning sun turns crimson.

To Master Ying, he reveals the treasury of one's own radiance. What need is there to ask whether coming and going is coming and going? From antiquity to the present, it has always been brilliantly manifest.
Brilliant! Without cultivation, without realization, all entanglements are severed. Hands and head are free and easy; the divine mechanism is alive. The crown of the head is majestic and grand;
the True Eye is opened. Huangbo struck Linji three times; he rolled like dust upon a level ground.
Shishi instructed his attendant:
"Within the sound of the three calls, one must personally grasp it; at every critical moment, never fail to act with what is appropriate.

At the place where the water from Kārtika’s bowl receives the needle, and when Yuanwu’s rooster flaps its wings—since time immemorial, this has never been obscured. From this point on, let there be nothing further within your breast."
Without doubt: Old Man Xi’s three-foot-long Vajra sword awaits its full deployment in years to come.
Sending off Chuwinei with a single blow strikes the very first pivot; it is enough to set a hairless iron hawk soaring. A wind whistles before the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.
Sā! Beyond the seven golden mountains, the sun shines brilliantly. How could it merely illuminate them entirely? It surely employs them in their entirety as well.
Moreover, there is ritual decorum and there is majestic authority. Return to your old garden for a brief rest; let not your resolve to travel for study ever falter.
I bid farewell to Venerable Xiù, whose name is the same as mine; truly fitting that he should shoulder this school with his whole being.

I am weary and ashamed that I lack the virtue of Perfect Illumination (Yuánzhào), yet there seems to be a wind from the Dharma Clouds (Fǎyún) in his extraordinary brilliance. When the golden hammer is brought down, there are no Buddhas; with the *zhílì* staff slung across his shoulder, he enters the mountains.
Wanfeng: "Set aside the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials. The courtyard is bright as the rain ceases, and the hibiscus is red.
To the *vina* (chant leader), he suddenly brandished his golden mallet: "Upon the peak of North Mountain, waves overturn the void. Who would discuss those with learning or those without?"
Study! Who asks about the penetration of the essence and the penetration of the teaching? Huangbo’s staff deceived Jibei; Cuoyan’s smile cheated Yunfeng.
You must know there is another transcendent realm: the Northern Dipper shifts west, the Southern Dipper moves east.

In mourning Master Qingchen Wai’an, I recall our friendship spanning thirty years. How many times we shared sleeping mats beneath the pines! You swept away the five teachings until not a single dharma remained;
you split the three mysteries into two sides. Suddenly, Guo Lang’s thread snapped, yet Sinu Ba’s cloth remains as it was.
Shan Chuan: Let the tattered hut follow the red flames; a single stalk of green thatch remains to brush the heavens.

Xie Fu has returned to his original state, yet as a physician in old age, he is increasingly beset by illness. How can one sustain this decaying illusion? To dispel the cold, one must rely on cotton from Mianzhou.

Appendix: To nourish the stomach, one still requires the ginseng of Shangdang. How could Sengqiao have lacked the arts to aid the world? Vimalakīrti possessed nothing but the resolve to benefit living beings.
Rising and sitting this morning, I am entirely as I was before; having finished writing this gāthā, I once again recite it to myself.

In presenting this record of the successive patriarchs’ transmission of the Dharma, it is simply this mind. It is luminously clear, with neither past nor present. The blossoming flowers and verdant willows are not other things;

the warbling of swallows and the singing of orioles are all the true sound. As for Yuanmeng’s serving of tea—how could he have reached it? Yet he struck the meditation seat to show his guests. However...
Capable and fit. When the Great Peng spreads its wings across ninety thousand *li*, who would say the misty waters of the Southern Abyss are deep?

As I see off the Abbot Sanchang, the rooster’s crowing fades; with a sudden turn of the body, he tramples the ocean of the Tripitaka and stirs up red dust. He soars through the layered heavens, a nine-crested phoenix in flight.
